haiku-low.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. The counter store is never touched, so no counter is read or written.
haiku-low.q2: The counts are keyed by customer ID, so all their keys share one budget: 100 requests per minute for Standard. Enterprise is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining 0. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. The script rejects without incrementing, so a 429 uses no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Budget is used at check time, and a backend failure does not refund it, so it stays counted.
haiku-low.q6: It is forwarded without being counted, a ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted, and the backend response is returned with no rate-limit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED, as product has not decided the limit.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis counter store, under key rl:<customerId>:<windowStart>. Each counter expires after 120 seconds, which removes old counts.
haiku-low.q9: Counts start again at each one-minute window boundary, using a new window key. Old counters expire after 120 seconds. Explicit reset behaviour beyond that is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q10: The check-and-count runs as one atomic Lua script on Redis, so no other command runs in the middle. The count can reach the limit but never pass it.
haiku-low.q11: It is the seconds until the window ends, computed by the Redis script from the server clock, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: Retrying the store is NOT STATED. The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. No counter is read or written; the counter store is never touched.
sonnet.q2: They share one budget, because counts are keyed by customer ID not API key. Total is the plan limit per window (100/min for Standard; Enterprise limit not decided). Note a boundary burst of up to 2x the limit across a window boundary is possible.
sonnet.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0. The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. On rejection the script does not increment, so a 429 uses no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Budget is used at check time and a backend failure does not refund it; the client gets the 500 with rate-limit headers.
sonnet.q6: The gateway fails open: forwards the request without counting it, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and returns the backend response with no rate-limit headers. (The script may still finish and count it anyway; accepted.)
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: not decided yet (either not enforced or a product-approved placeholder until set).
sonnet.q8: In the shared Redis counter store, one counter per customer per window under key rl:<customerId>:<windowStart>. Each counter expires after 120 seconds, which removes old counts.
sonnet.q9: Windows are fixed one-minute periods; counts start again at each minute boundary (window start taken from the Redis server clock), so budget resets at the next window. A new counter key is used per window.
sonnet.q10: A Redis Lua script runs atomically in one step on the server (read count, reject if at/above limit, else increment), so two instances racing for the last slot cannot both be admitted; count can reach but never pass the limit.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After is the seconds until the window ends (returned by the Redis script), rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether the gateway retries the store (the document says it forwards the request without counting). The client gets no X-RateLimit headers, just the backend response.
